title: Omnes' rules
summary: Check whether your menu prices are well spread between cheap, medium and expensive.

what: Once prices are set, the menu should be spread harmoniously between cheap, medium and expensive items, with suitable options for your customers.
Omnes' rules are four commercial principles: price proportionality, item count per zone, fit between offered and demanded prices, and where to place the daily special.
formula: Proportionality: most expensive price ≤ 2 to 3 × cheapest price
Width of each zone = (most expensive − cheapest) ÷ 3
Balanced menu: half of the items in the medium zone and a quarter at each end
Average ticket within ±10% of the average menu price
Daily special in the medium price zone

variables.name: Average menu price
variables.description: The sum of all menu prices divided by the number of items.

variables.name: Zones
variables.description: Three ranges of the same width: cheap, medium and expensive.

steps: Find the cheapest and the most expensive price, and compare the ratio between them.
Split the difference into three equal zones.
Count how many items fall into each zone.
Work out the average menu price and compare it with the average ticket.
Check which zone the daily special is in.

examples.title: Bakery with 16 cakes
paragraphs: Prices go from $40 to $115: a $75 difference, so zones are $25 wide.
Cheap: $40 to $65; medium: over $65 up to $90; expensive: over $90 up to $115.
A balanced menu has 4 cheap, 8 medium and 4 expensive items.
If the average price is $77.50, a healthy average ticket goes from $69.75 to $85.25.

notes.text: Customers move within certain price ranges according to their income: a business can't be expensive and cheap at the same time.
If you compete on price, list prices in a column on the right of the menu; if you compete on product, place the price close to the dish description.

average-ticket.label: Average ticket
average-ticket.placeholder: What each customer pays per item on average (e.g. 80)

steps.zone-width: Width of each zone = (most expensive − cheapest) ÷ 3 = ({maxPrice} − {minPrice}) ÷ 3 = {zoneWidth}
steps.zones: Cheap: {minPrice} to {lowZoneMax} · Medium: up to {mediumZoneMax} · Expensive: up to {maxPrice}
steps.distribution: Items per zone: {low} cheap, {medium} medium, {high} expensive
steps.average-price: Average price = sum of prices ÷ count = {total} ÷ {count} = {averagePrice}

choices.ideal: Ideal: the most expensive costs up to twice the cheapest
choices.acceptable: Acceptable: the most expensive costs 2 to 3 times the cheapest
choices.too-wide: Too wide: the most expensive is more than 3 times the cheapest
choices.balanced: Suitable: the average ticket is within ±10% of the average price
choices.too-expensive: Prices too high: customers spend less than 90% of the average
choices.too-cheap: Prices too low: customers spend more than 110% of the average
choices.low: In the cheap zone (it should be in the medium one)
choices.medium: In the medium zone, as it should
choices.high: In the expensive zone (it should be in the medium one)
choices.distribution-balanced: Balanced: the medium zone has as many items as the other two combined
choices.distribution-unbalanced: Unbalanced: the medium zone should have as many items as the other two combined

labels.prices-hint: Write one price per line (you can also separate them with spaces or semicolons).
